intro: Professionals and everyday users convert miles (mi) to nautical miles (nmi) when working across imperial and other standards in architectural blueprints, international manufacturing tolerances, athletic track distances, and hardware sizing. One mile (statute) equals 0.868976 nautical miles, while 1 nautical mile equals 1.150779 miles. Whether you are verifying length specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor vs. Early Rounding Drift
items: The exact conversion factor from Mile (Statute) to Nautical Mile is 0.86897624, derived from the 1959 International Yard and Pound Agreement (1 inch = 25.4 mm, 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg).

In structural engineering, CNC machining, or bulk inventory totals, rounding the multiplier to 2 decimal places too early can introduce cumulative tolerance errors; always compute with the full factor and round only the final displayed figure.

faqs.question: How many nautical miles (nmi) are in 1 mile (statute) (mi)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.86897624 nautical miles (nmi) in 1 mile (statute) (mi), which rounds to 0.869 nmi for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 nautical mile equals 1.150779 miles.

faqs.question: How do I convert miles to nautical miles (mi to nmi)?
faqs.answer: To convert miles to nautical miles, use the formula: nmi = mi × 0.86897624. For example, converting 15 mi gives 13.0346 nmi.

faqs.question: What is 15 miles in nautical miles?
faqs.answer: 15 miles (mi) equals exactly 13.0346 nautical miles (nmi) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
